title: 曝光情感行业骗子《真实社交》欺诈学员……

timeline.summary: A third-party man says newer team members lacked his years of preparation; channel-added yellow subtitles challenge whether his mentors are still apprentices.
He says they were taught by him and that he needed to help create traffic for them; inserted profile screenshots compare claimed experience.
Editorial captions condemn the explanation as supporting fabrication; the man says he allowed them to act and financially supported them.
The monologue names Cim, ZK and Hank and argues that whatever material they release only proves Jackson is a good person; the editor responds mockingly.
The man says the purpose was to let his people start accounts and earn money quickly; the short closes with mocking student/clown and harvesting-grass imagery.

claims.speaker: third-party man, identity alleged by the short but not independently verified
claims.statement: He says he permitted team members to perform/act and financially supported them so they could create traffic, start accounts and make money quickly.
claims.conditions: Selected and edited excerpt; '演' may describe staged promotional content, but the full source and contractual context are absent.

claims.speaker: channel editor / burned-in yellow subtitles
claims.statement: The editor interprets the excerpt as proof that Jackson supported mentors fabricating cases and deceiving students.
claims.conditions: Reputational accusation and editorial inference, not a verified fact or spoken admission by Mikey in the clip.

visual_findings: All sampled and one-second frames show one third-party speaker, two profile-description screenshots, channel-added white/yellow subtitles, a reaction insert and a mocking closing graphic.
The screenshots demonstrate what the editor displayed, not that the profiles are authentic, current or written by the people alleged.
White subtitles generally follow the man's speech; yellow subtitles are adversarial commentary and must not be merged with his words or automatically attributed to Mikey.

permissions.reason: Same restricted dispute material already represented; named-person allegations, edited context and speaker identity remain unverified.

limitations: No original unedited monologue or response from all named parties was obtained.
Automatic ASR has name and wording errors.
The short cannot establish fraud, victimhood, financial harm, intent or legal liability.
